# Modules

maisys's built-in modules, and the keys you can set for each one. Each module is a table in profile and machine files, named after the module. Modules are off until a file turns them on with `enabled = true`. The exception is [sudo](#sudo), which has no `enabled` key: its `nopasswd` key turns it on.

A machine's config is built in layers: each module's defaults (listed below), then each profile in the order the machine file lists them, then the machine file itself. The layers are merged like this:

- **Single values:** the last layer that sets a value wins.
- **Tables,** including tables keyed by name such as `files.items`: merged key by key, so a later layer only needs the keys it changes. A new entry in a table keyed by name starts from the defaults listed for its keys.
- **Lists that are "combined across layers":** each layer adds its items to the list, leaving out duplicates and keeping the order. A later layer can't remove an item.
- **Other lists:** replaced by the later layer.

Keys are case-sensitive, and an unknown key is an error. Editors that support JSON schemas for TOML can complete and check keys with `config.schema.json`, which is published with each release: point to it with a `#:schema` line at the top of the file.

## Machine and profile files

Besides the module tables, these keys go at the top of machine and profile files.

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `profiles` | list of strings | Machine files only. The profiles to apply before the machine file, in order, by their file names in profiles/ without .toml. |
| `os` | string | The operating system: "fedora", "ubuntu" or "windows". Every machine file sets it. A profile that sets it can only be used by machines with that OS. |
| `os_version` | string | Machine files only, optional. The OS version, such as "44" or "26.04". maisys refuses to run on any other version. |
| `arch` | string | Linux machine files only, optional. The CPU architecture: "amd64" or "arm64". maisys refuses to run on any other architecture. |

## sudo

Lets your user run sudo without a password.

Works on Fedora and Ubuntu.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sudo.nopasswd` | boolean | `false` | `nopasswd` lets your user run sudo without a password, through a rule in /etc/sudoers.d that is checked with visudo before it's installed. Turning it off deletes that rule again, unless your user isn't in the wheel or sudo group, which would leave them without sudo. |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `packages.enabled` | boolean | `false` | `enabled` turns the module on. |
| `packages.install` | list of strings | `[]` | `install` lists the packages to install and keep up to date, by the names the machine's OS uses for them. Combined across layers: profiles and the machine file add to the list instead of replacing it. |

## files

Copies files, directories and templates from the config repo into your home folder, and reports files changed since.

Works on Fedora, Ubuntu and Windows.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `files.enabled` | boolean | `false` | `enabled` turns the module on. |
| `files.vars` | table of strings |  | `vars` holds values for templates, which read them as .Vars. |
| `files.items` | table of tables |  | `items` are the files and directories to copy, each under a name you choose. A later profile or the machine file can change one item, or turn it off with enabled = false, without repeating the rest. |
| `files.items.<name>.enabled` | boolean | `true` | `enabled` copies the item. Items are on unless turned off. |
| `files.items.<name>.source` | string | `""` | `source` is the path in the config repo. A directory is copied file by file, and files in the target directory that don't come from it are left alone. |
| `files.items.<name>.target` | string | `""` | `target` is where the item goes, inside your home folder, such as "\~/.gitconfig". A directory can also go in "\~/" itself. On Windows, \~ is %USERPROFILE%. |
| `files.items.<name>.template` | boolean | `false` | `template` renders the source as a Go text/template, which can use .Vars, .Facts and .Machine. |
| `files.items.<name>.mode` | string | `""` | `mode` sets the permissions, such as "0600". Without it, files keep the executable bit they have in the config repo. |
| `files.items.<name>.eol` | string | `""` | `eol` set to "crlf" converts line endings to CRLF, for Windows programs that need them. Without it, line endings stay as they are in the config repo. |

## golang

Installs the Go toolchain, and Go programs with go install.

Works on Fedora and Ubuntu.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `golang.enabled` | boolean | `false` | `enabled` turns the module on. |
| `golang.version` | string | `"latest"` | `version` to install: "latest" (the default) for the newest stable release, or an exact version such as "1.2.3" to pin it. |
| `golang.tools` | list of strings | `[]` | `tools` lists Go programs to install with go install, as a package path and a version, such as "mvdan.cc/gofumpt@latest". ## wsl

Sets up a Linux distro running in WSL: /etc/wsl.conf, opening links in Windows, and optionally the Windows Git Credential Manager.

Works on Fedora and Ubuntu.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wsl.enabled` | boolean | `false` | `enabled` turns the module on. |
| `wsl.systemd` | boolean | `true` | `systemd` runs systemd in the distro. |
| `wsl.wslg` | boolean | `true` | `wslg` shows Linux GUI apps with WSLg. Set it to false to use X410 instead, through a bridge service maisys sets up. |
| `wsl.append_windows_path` | boolean | `true` | `append_windows_path` adds the Windows PATH to the end of the distro's PATH. |
| `wsl.git_credential_manager` | boolean | `false` | `git_credential_manager` makes git use the Windows Git Credential Manager, so the distro shares the sign-ins Windows has. It needs Git for Windows. |

## wsl_host

Installs and updates WSL, writes .wslconfig, and creates and sets up distros.

Works on Windows.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wsl_host.enabled` | boolean | `false` | `enabled` turns the module on. |
| `wsl_host.default_distro` | string | `""` | `default_distro` is the distro WSL starts by default: one of distros. |
| `wsl_host.config_url` | string | `""` | `config_url` is the HTTPS URL new distros clone the config repo from. Without it, they use this machine's own config URL, which must then be HTTPS. |
| `wsl_host.wslconfig` | table |  | `wslconfig` sets keys in %USERPROFILE%\\.wslconfig. Keys left out aren't written, so WSL's defaults apply. Changes take effect after wsl --shutdown. |
| `wsl_host.wslconfig.memory` | string | `""` | `memory` is the most memory WSL can use, such as "16GB". |
| `wsl_host.wslconfig.processors` | integer | `0` | `processors` is the number of processors WSL can use. |
| `wsl_host.wslconfig.swap` | string | `""` | `swap` is the size of WSL's swap file, such as "8GB", or "0" for none. |
| `wsl_host.wslconfig.networking_mode` | string | `""` | `networking_mode` is "nat" or "mirrored". |
| `wsl_host.wslconfig.auto_memory_reclaim` | string | `""` | `auto_memory_reclaim` is how WSL gives unused memory back to Windows: "disabled", "gradual" or "dropcache". |
| `wsl_host.wslconfig.dns_tunneling` | boolean | `false` | `dns_tunneling` answers WSL's DNS requests through Windows. |
| `wsl_host.distros` | table of tables |  | `distros` are the distros to create, by distro name. Each is created and set up once, then kept up to date by running maisys sync inside it. Distros are never deleted or recreated. |
| `wsl_host.distros.<name>.image` | string | `""` | `image` is what to install, by its name in wsl --list --online, such as "FedoraLinux-44". It must match the machine's os, and os_version if set. It's only used when the distro is created. |
| `wsl_host.distros.<name>.machine` | string | `""` | `machine` is the Linux machine file maisys applies inside the distro. |
| `wsl_host.distros.<name>.user` | string | `""` | `user` is the Linux user to create, in the wheel or sudo group. It gets a random password, shown once when the distro is created, which you should change with passwd. For the first sync inside the distro only, maisys adds a temporary rule that lets it use sudo without the password; set sudo.nopasswd in the machine file to keep that. |
